correctness.rationale: All edges of the cubical bipolar polytope are exactly cover relations of the cube face lattice; the nonempty-face graph is the Cartesian product of n three-vertex paths, with the empty-face vertex adjacent to precisely the 2^n cube vertices. Any shortest path either stays within that product or uses the pole once, giving the minimum-of-two-routes formula. Rearrangement of the two path lengths proves the sharp diameter and the exact diametral configurations. Coordinate multinomial enumeration yields the full distance polynomial. The exponential-moment argument proves the all-dimension mean-distance bound. An independent graph/BFS construction and an independent multinomial count agreed in n=1,...,6 (the exhaustive finite checks are supplementary).

value.rationale: Pavlík introduced a natural new all-dimensional geometric family; its complete shortest-path structure is a meaningful missing invariant. The pole produces a sharp, nontrivial two-route metric, self-centered graphs in every dimension, irregular for n>=2, a closed enumerator for every distance and all diametral pairs, and a quantifiable asymptotic collapse of mean distances from 8n/9 in the direct graph to 2n/3+2. These are substantive structural and asymptotic statements, not a mere restatement of cube face counts.
